(5.4) Here 1 ≪ H means only that H is bounded below by a positive constant. In these low-height assertions the derivatives of W are bounded independently of X. 3. Suppose u = ±t + u0, T ≤ |t| ≤ 2T, 2T + |u0| ≤ X0.17, and |∂jW| ≪j LCj for fixed C. For every fixed K > 0, if T ≥ LCt with Ct sufficiently large, then Z T≤|t|≤2T X a WA(a)|F±t+u0 (a)|2 dt T ≤ Z T≤|t|≤2T DW dt T + O(QL−K ), (5.5) where the exact diagonal is DW = X b |βb|2 X (a,b)=1 WA(a). No lower bound on H is required here. When B ≤ X0.40 the restriction on u0 can be omitted. There is also an absolute sufficiently small γ > 0 such that, when B ≤ X0.40, T ≫ X0.01, and |∂jW| ≪j Xjγ, the corresponding estimate is Z T≤|t|≤2T X a WA(a)|F±t+u0 (a)|2 dt T ≤ Z T≤|t|≤2T DW dt T + O(QX−10γ ). (5.6) This γ is independent of the fixed powers in the divisor bounds. In the last two estimates, a radial support of width O(J−1) gives DW ≪ A J X b |βb|2 for J ≤ LO(1), or J ≤ Xγ, respectively. In particular, when B ≤ X0.40, the coefficients may be restricted sharply to any norm cell without changing these assertions.
